title: How Tibo Louis-Lucas bootstrapped 5 AI products to $1M+/month: ship fast, charge early, SEO tools
summary: Tibo explains how he runs five AI businesses with a tiny team: validate with revenue from day one, ship many cheap experiments, stay in constant contact with users, and follow unexpected usage into pivots (product videos to Rabbit). He covers pricing at $50-100/month, churn thresholds, tool-based SEO, and building with AI in Cursor.

principles.text: Don't force-sell to avoid being wrong; stay open to signals that a bigger opportunity exists and pivot.
principles.quote: it's more important for them to not be wrong than being successful. And so what you do in these cases you're trying to force sell.

principles.text: Talk to users constantly; when people twist your product into another use, follow that signal.
principles.quote: When you have a product that is made for one thing and people are actually twisting it to turn into this other thing, that's usually a very strong signal that you have to follow.

principles.text: Validate with revenue from day one; without sticky revenue, other signals are self-deception.
principles.quote: if there is no revenue, there's no stickiness in the revenue, it's going to be very hard to build a successful business.

principles.text: Price at $50-100/month to attract high-quality, low-churn customers and position as premium, not cheap.
principles.quote: I feel that's the perfect amount from 50 to 100 per month because it's not too much, so people do not ask me for quotes before signing up

principles.text: Monthly churn above ~20% means the product isn't sticky; fix retention before investing in acquisition.
principles.quote: I would consider everything um better than than 20% churn, like monthly churn.

principles.text: Ship many small experiments quickly; quantity of attempts leads to better outcomes than polishing one.
principles.quote: we were shipping one new project per per week uh until something stick.
